items.title: WM Senibong's RM6.7bil development pipeline underpinned by AA-IS sukuk rating
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: WM Senibong Bhd's financial standing and development prospects have received a boost after its wholly-owned subsidiary, WM Senibong Capital Bhd, secured an affirmation of its AA-IS rating with a stable outlook from MARC Ratings Bhd. MARC's rating affirmation is underpinned by WM Senibong's sizeable unbilled sales of RM651.5 million and planned development launches with a combined gross development value (GDV) of RM6.7 billion, providing earnings visibility through 2030. WM Senibong's executive director and chief executive officer Quay Chew Keong said, "The reaffirmation of the rating by MARC Ratings is a strong testament to WM Senibong's solid business fundamentals, disciplined financial management and proven track record in delivering quality developments."

items.title: Health Ministry faces shortage of 1,176 drivers, including ambulance personnel
items.summary: Berita Harian reported that the ministry attributed the shortage to delays in recruiting General Service Assistants (Driving) after the Public Service Department temporarily suspended recruitment through the Public Services Commission (PSC) in 2024 to facilitate implementation of the new Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA). Under the SSPA, the former vehicle driver scheme was merged into the new General Service Assistant scheme, requiring recruitment requirements to be reviewed, particularly for personnel tasked with driving ambulances. As of September 30, the ministry had 8,863 General Service Assistant (Driving) positions, of which 7,687 were filled, according to figures provided by MoH to Berita Harian.

items.title: PN will not sign CSA, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: He said the agreement, initiated by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, had sidelined PN as a coalition and opposition bloc. Takiyuddin said the CSA was an individual decision by the MPs involved and did not represent PN's official position. He said those involved included a Bersatu faction, former Bersatu members and the Malaysian United Democratic Alliance (Muda).

items.title: Malaysia's manufacturing sector returns to growth in October, PMI at 51.0
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's manufacturing sector recorded a renewed improvement in its health in October 2026, with the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rising to 51.0 during the month, signalling a return to growth on the back of stronger new orders and output. Economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence Maryam Baluch said the latest PMI data pointed to an improving picture for Malaysia's manufacturing sector at the start of the final quarter. "New orders returned to growth, supported in part by stronger demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related products and underpinned a fresh rise in output," she said in a note.

items.title: Sympathy scam: Teo urges vigilance against AI-generated fake donation appeals
items.summary: KULAI: Social media users are urged to enhance their digital literacy and remain vigilant against the latest "sympathy scam", a fraudulent scheme that is becoming increasingly sophisticated by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI) technology. Deputy Minister of Communications Teo Nie Ching said unscrupulous individuals are misusing AI advances to manipulate distressing situations and elicit public sympathy to run fake donation drives. Teo said the ministry had also received complaints from individuals whose photographs and names were used without permission to solicit donations.

items.title: Malaysia banks ride investment-led growth, but deposit war threatens margins
items.summary: PublicInvest Research and CIMB Securities maintained "Overweight" calls on the sector, citing healthy loan growth and resilient fundamentals, while Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research retained its "Neutral" stance, citing limited upside from current valuations. According to PublicInvest, system-wide loans grew 6.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in September 2026, driven by a 7.7 per cent expansion in business loans. PublicInvest Research and CIMB Securities reported system deposit growth of 3.7 per cent YoY in September, compared with 4.2 per cent in August.

items.title: Judge denies Trump admin attempt to block key Senate result
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A federal judge on Sunday tossed out an extremely unusual attempt by US President Donald Trump's administration to hold up midterm election results in Alaska should the Democratic Senate candidate win. The Department of Justice (DOJ) had asked the court to block certification of the results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses on Tuesday, because a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan would have drawn away votes. According to Trump and the lawsuit, the Democratic candidate in Alaska, Mary Peltola, has tried to get an unfair advantage by recruiting another person named Sullivan to run and confuse voters who intended to back the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan.

items.title: Takiyuddin: Perikatan not part of Bersatu MPs’ CSA, won’t sign deal just for allocations
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 2 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) was not involved in negotiations for the confidence-and-supply agreement (CSA) signed by six Bersatu MPs with the federal government and will not enter such a deal merely to secure constituency allocations, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reportedly said. Coincidentally, those who joined the CSA are from groups that are not actively involved in PN, namely Bersatu itself, former Bersatu members who previously switched parties, and Muda,” he was quoted as saying. Six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin signed the CSA on October 29 alongside Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six former Bersatu MPs who now sit as independents.

items.title: Mi Technovation's S$104mil Singapore hub to anchor next phase of AI, EV powertrain growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd's (MiTB) proposed S$103.9 million (RM331.8 million) acquisition of a seven-storey industrial building in Singapore is a strategic move to support the commercialisation of its intelligent electric powertrain systems and autonomous driving platforms. Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) views the acquisition of KHL building through its wholly owned subsidiary, Ohima International Pte Ltd, as a long-term strategic investment rather than a conventional property purchase. Management is targeting deliveries of 45 to 55 powertrain systems this year, with 27 units already secured year-to-date, PublicInvest said.

items.title: South Korea to double spending on AI and chips in 2027
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea will double spending on artificial intelligence and semiconductors in 2027 to a record high of US$16 billion, President Lee Jae Myung said Monday in his annual budget speech to parliament. "We will allocate 21.3 trillion won (US$16 billion) to semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centres, the 'three mega-projects', as well as investment in artificial intelligence, nearly double this year's amount," Lee said. Overall, the budget plan totals 821 trillion won, a 12.8 per cent increase from this year, making it the largest budget proposal on record.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN targets 15,000 flags in Tangga Batu as campaign gathers pace
items.summary: MELAKA: The BN election machinery in Tangga Batu is preparing to put up 15,000 flags, although the campaign's traditional flag war has yet to gather pace. The flag installation exercise, led by the BN Youth machinery, covers four state constituencies: Sungai Udang, Klebang, Pantai Kundor and Paya Rumput. Tangga Batu BN chairman Datuk Rais Yasin said the relatively quiet campaign, including the absence of large-scale flag displays, did not mean the party's machinery was inactive.

items.title: DAP confirms seven seats for Sarawak polls, mulls Batu Lintang as eighth
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 2 — DAP will contest seven seats in Kuching and Bau areas in the upcoming 13th Sarawak State Election, said its state chairman Chong Chieng Jen. According to Chong, who chaired the party’s state committee meeting earlier yesterday, the seven confirmed seats are Padungan, Pending, Batu Kitang, Kota Sentosa, Batu Kawah, Tasik Biru and Opar. Ruling coalition Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) swept 76 of the 82 seats contested, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats.

items.title: ‘Do not be discouraged’: Anwar backs Hakim Danish after fourth-place Moto3 finish
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has offered words of encouragement to young Malaysian rider Muhammad Hakim Danish Ramli after he finished fourth in the Moto3 race at the Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit yesterday. “Congratulations to Hakim Danish for finishing fourth in the Moto3 race! There are still races remaining, so keep pushing to go further,” he said in a post on X. Anwar said that besides Hakim Danish, he also took time to meet young Malaysian riders Muhammad Qabil Irfan Azlan, Qayyim Razin Razali and Muhammad Naqib Rifqi Zulhelmi.

items.title: KL police investigate after woman allegedly assaults two children at shopping mall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police are investigating the incident involving an unknown woman who shoved and hit two children at a shopping mall here yesterday. Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said they found a 35-second video that went viral on social media depicting an argument between two individuals following the incident, adding that the father of a child involved in the incident, aged 36, lodged a police report at 7.39pm. He also advised the public to refrain from speculating and urged those with information to contact the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, the Dang Wangi district police headquarters at 03-2600 2222 or the nearest police station.

items.title: HLIB retains 'Buy' on UEM Sunrise as RM4bil industrial JV unlocks Johor landbank
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its "Buy" recommendation on UEM Sunrise Bhd, with an unchanged target price of 92 sen, based on a 60 per cent discount to its estimated revalued net asset value (RNAV) of RM2.30. UEM Sunrise is stepping up efforts to monetise its Johor landbank through a 50:50 joint venture (JV) with AME Elite Consortium Bhd to develop a RM4 billion integrated managed industrial park in Gerbang Nusajaya, Iskandar Puteri. The partnership involves UEM Sunrise disposing of 402.1 acres of freehold land to the JV, via Gerbang Synergy Sdn Bhd, for RM972.1 million, or RM55.50 per sq ft.

items.title: Australian home prices fall for seventh month, looming rate hike adds to pain
items.summary: Figures on Monday from property data firm Cotality showed national home prices fell 1.2 per cent in October from September, when they dropped by a downward revised figure of 1.3 per cent. That left values 6.7 per cent below their peak and down 2.8 per cent from a year ago. Sydney prices fell 1.6 per cent in the month, leaving values 1.5 per cent below where they were five years ago.

items.title: No unhealthy API readings recorded nationwide this morning
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: No areas in the country recorded unhealthy air quality as at 7.30am today. According to the latest data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 44 monitoring stations recorded moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across 11 states and two federal territories. Another 24 monitoring stations recorded good API readings.

items.title: TSH Resources agrees to Singapore haze assessment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd has offered to engage assessors from a Singapore government panel at its own expense amid investigations into forest fires in Indonesia linked to transboundary haze. The plantation group said it had written to Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) confirming its willingness to have its operations, corporate relationships and supply chains assessed. The move follows notices issued by NEA to its two Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries, TSH Oversea Pte Ltd and TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd, under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014.

items.title: Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to boost industry competitiveness, protect jobs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Media Innovation Fund 2.0 will help strengthen the competitiveness and technological capabilities of local media companies while ensuring industry sustainability. Malaysian Media Council (MMC) chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan said the fund was timely as media organisations struggled to keep pace with rapid technological advancements, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, intense competition from digital platforms, and changing news consumption habits. Meanwhile, Media Chinese International Limited (MCIL) (Malaysia) Group editor-in-chief Datuk Kuik Cheng Kang said the fund reflected the government's commitment to helping media organisations chart a new direction while protecting workers' welfare.

items.title: Health Ministry faces 1,176-driver shortage, including for ambulances
items.summary: The ministry attributed the shortage to delays in filling General Services Assistant (Driving) positions following the temporary suspension of recruitment by the Public Service Department (PSD) through the Public Services Commission (PSC) in 2024. "Under the new system, the former vehicle driver scheme has been consolidated into a new scheme known as General Services Assistant (Driving), under the Skills Services classification (H). The ministry expects vacancies for General Services Assistant (Driving) positions at public healthcare facilities nationwide to be filled in stages from April 2027.

items.title: Teenage girl falls from second floor of Tampoi flat after suffering seizure
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 2 — A teenage girl sustained injuries after having a seizure while peering over a staircase wall, before falling from the second floor of a flat in the Tampoi area here yesterday. Acting Johor Bahru Utara district police chief Supt Azrol Anuar Nor said his team received a report at about 12.20pm regarding the incident involving the 18-year-old victim. He said the victim was found lying conscious on the sidewalk beside the flat building.

items.title: Kalimaran festival celebrates Murut heritage, strengthens ties with other communities
items.summary: TENOM: The Kalimaran festival celebrates the cultural heritage of Sabah's Murut community while fostering closer ties with other ethnic groups. Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang said the festival originated from Injawari or Panawari, a traditional gathering held by the Murut community before independence during British colonial rule. "The festival's long history shows that Murut cultural heritage has deep traditional roots and must be preserved as a symbol of the community's identity and pride," he said at the 20th Kalimaran festival in Kemabong near here recently.

items.title: Inmates taken from Klang rehab centre: Police open criminal trespass probe
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — Police are investigating a trespassing case involving a group suspected of removing several inmates from a private rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, near here, without the management's permission. Klang Utara police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the rehabilitation centre’s owner on October 28 that a group of unknown men and women had entered the premises and taken several inmates away. Following the incident, Ramsay advised the public not to speculate on the case because it could threaten public order and disrupt police investigations.

items.title: Poor nutrition puts Malaysian children's long-term health at risk
items.summary: The findings of the second South-East Asian Nutrition Surveys (SEANUTS II) Malaysia showed that 94.8 per cent of children had inadequate vitamin D intake, while 79.4 per cent did not meet the recommended calcium intake. The research sampled 2,989 children aged 0.5 to 12.9 years, representing roughly 4.9 million children in that age group across Peninsular Malaysia. The survey recorded 8.9 per cent of children experiencing stunting, 6.7 per cent wasting, 9.2 per cent overweight, and 8.8 per cent obesity.

items.title: Man smashes five bank machines after failed ATM withdrawal in Sarikei, injures one person
items.summary: SARIKEI, Nov 2 — Angered after failing to withdraw cash from an automated teller machine (ATM), a man vandalised five banking machines using a machete before allegedly injuring a young man who tried to stop him in an incident on Jalan Masjid Lama, near here, early yesterday morning. Sarikei district police chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the 38-year-old suspect is believed to have damaged two ATM machines, two cash deposit machines (CDM), and one cheque deposit machine at a bank around 12.05am. “The suspect then surrendered at the Sarikei police station and the police also seized a Toyota Hilux and a machete believed to have been used in the incident,” he said.

items.title: OPEC+ to maintain oil output for third consecutive month in December
items.summary: "The seven participating countries decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026," the statement noted. Under the agreement, the seven countries will maintain their combined required production level at approximately 31.01 million barrel per day (bpd) in December. Saudi Arabia's required production level will remain at 10.48 million bpd, followed by Russia at 9.95 million bpd and Iraq at 4.43 million bpd.

items.title: Tesla, Samsung oppose new US tariffs on Vietnam as probe deadline nears
items.summary: HANOI: Businesses are divided over whether Washington should propose new tariffs on Vietnamese goods this month, with Tesla and Samsung not in favour, while others have called for penalties, submissions to the US government show. The US has accused Vietnam of "a persistent failure to resolve long-standing concerns about IP protection and enforcement." Vietnam has urged Washington to conduct its investigations objectively.

items.title: Malaysia’s first FA-50M jets arrive at Kuantan base for final acceptance tests
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 2 — Two FA-50M aircraft arrived at the airbase here yesterday, marking the first delivery of the 18 aircraft to be acquired by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) from Korea Aerospace Industries. According to a post on the RMAF’s Facebook page, the aircraft departed Labuan Air Base at 1.45pm and landed at the Kuantan Airbase at 3.38pm, witnessed by Chief of Air Force General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris. Also present to witness the historic occasion were Deputy Chief of Air Force Lieutenant General Datuk Seri Nur Hafis Abdul Karim, Air Education and Training Commander Lieutenant General Datuk Mohd Sani Omar, and Air Support Commander Major General Datuk Ahmad Khusairi Ahmad Fadli.

items.title: ‘See you again at Sepang’: Anwar hails Malaysian MotoGP and thanks fans, organisers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated and thanked all staff, organisers, and motorsports fans for successfully hosting the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP), which ended yesterday at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). In a post on his official Facebook page, Anwar described this year's edition as thrilling and vibrant, featuring fierce competition among the world's top riders and memorable moments throughout the event. See you again at Sepang,” he said.

items.title: #NSTviral: Deepavali kolam displays draw praise at shopping malls [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Shopping malls are drawing praise for their Deepavali decorations, with social media users welcoming the festive displays and the attention given to the celebration. Threads user sabrinalailysobri said she looked forward to seeing different cultural celebrations, from Deepavali kolam decorations to Chinese New Year dragon dances. "When it's Deepavali, I get excited to see the kolam decorations.

items.title: Dollar rangebound ahead of US midterms; bitcoin reels from crypto heist
items.summary: In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin and ether were nursing losses following last week's record US$6.3 billion heist at Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange. Traders were bracing for a packed week dominated by the US midterm elections, October US jobs data and central bank rate decisions in the UK, Australia, Norway and Sweden. Sterling was little changed at US$1.3387, while the dollar steadied at 101.94 against a basket of currencies.

items.title: Asia shares bend under AI stress; Apple earnings loom
items.summary: At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth of nearly 30 per cent in 2026, slowing to 18 per cent next year. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.5 per cent, while South Korea lost 0.8 per cent, having shed 16 per cent last month. MORE RATE HIKES COMING On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures edged up 0.4 per cent, while Nasdaq futures bounced 0.6 per cent.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher on expectations of OPR normalisation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and major currencies on Monday, supported by expectations of a possible overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting this Thursday. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid opined that the MPC members would decide to raise the OPR by 25 basis points (bps). He said the pre-emptive rate cut in July 2025, which lowered the OPR from three per cent to 2.75 per cent, had served its purpose, as concerns over slower economic growth following the tariff shock had not materialised.

items.title: Police probe residents' escape from Klang rehabilitation centre
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police are investigating the disappearance of several residents from a private drug and alcohol rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, Klang, after its owner reported that a group of men and women had taken them away without the management's permission last week. Klang Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the centre's owner on Oct 28. He said the owner reported that a group of men and women had arrived at the premises and taken several residents away without the management's permission.

items.title: Bank of England poised to raise rates but may push back on bets for more
items.summary: MANCHESTER: The Bank of England (BoE) is expected to bow to inflation pressure from soaring energy costs and raise interest rates on Thursday, though it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year. Economists polled by Reuters expect the BoE to raise Bank Rate to four per cent from 3.75 per cent, its first hike since August 2023, when inflation was still more than triple its two per cent target. Inflation has since run hotter than the BoE expected.

items.title: Official: Four US citizens, Canadian among Spain train crash dead
items.summary: MADRID, (Spain): Four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed in last week's high-speed train collision in Spain, authorities said. Wednesday's disaster — one of Europe's deadliest rail accidents this century — has seen victims' relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts. Three reports for missing people remain active, the authorities said.

items.title: Oil slips more than 1pct as talks continue on ending Iran war
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell US$1.59, or 1.40 per cent, to US$111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$102.56 a barrel, down US$1.56, or 1.50 per cent. Brent ended October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the US-Iran conflict could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections. However, the market remained alert to the possibility that rhetoric around Iran could be ratcheted higher and push Brent toward US$120 after the midterm elections, Waterer said.

items.title: Sarawak's economic paradox
items.summary: Yet its median gross monthly household income was RM5,504, compared with Malaysia's RM7,017. Its mean household income, RM6,947, was also below the national average of RM9,155. Using 2024 provides a common reference year for production and household income.

items.title: The case of Maxis – U Mobile merger
items.summary: The rumour mill is back spinning with the story of a merger between Maxis Bhd and U Mobile Sdn Bhd. A merged Maxis-U Mobile entity would overtake CelcomDigi Bhd as the country's largest mobile operator by subscribers. U Mobile operates Malaysia's second 5G network alongside Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB).

items.title: Simpan SSPN 'one of the best' for savings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians have deposited RM26.07 billion in savings into the National Higher Education Fund Corporation's (PTPTN) Simpan SSPN, with 7.74 million accounts recorded up to Sept 30, says its chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim. She said the figures underscored Simpan SSPN's continued relevance as a savings scheme for higher education in Malaysia. Simpan SSPN encourages Malaysians to save early for their children's higher education, helping to reduce the reliance on education loans.

items.title: Why Malaysia should have national long-term care insurance and how it can be funded
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — If Malaysia introduces a new nationwide insurance to cover the cost of long-term care of older persons, who would be paying for it? But wait, just what is long-term care insurance? Unlike a medical card or medical insurance which covers hospital bills, long-term care insurance covers the care and support that a person — including older persons — needs outside of hospitals.

items.title: Off the trail, into danger: Mount Kinabalu guides warn trespassers of the price rescuers pay
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 2 — Security controls at Kinabalu Park are adequate, but trespassing on prohibited trails on Mount Kinabalu puts mountain guides at risk of physical injury and adds to the burden of search and rescue (SAR) operations. Kinabalu Mountain Guides Association chairman Danson Bulangai said restricted areas had been marked with red paint along the park boundaries, with warning signs and references to the relevant legal provisions at every sub-station to deter trespassing. “Using unauthorised trails endangers both mountain guides and the individuals involved, who face risks including physical injury, exposure to extreme weather and altitude sickness.

items.title: Online renewal for 10-year Malaysian passports starts tomorrow
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Passport renewal services through the MyOnline Passport system will offer a choice of five- or 10-year validity periods starting tomorrow. The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM), in a Facebook post, said the new facility allows applicants to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs. “This initiative provides greater flexibility and convenience for Malaysians to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs,” according to JIM.

items.title: Selangor schools open as usual tomorrow but parents may keep children home if concerned over haze, says state education dept
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 1 — All schools in Selangor will operate as usual tomorrow, according to the Selangor Education Department (JPN). In a statement today, the department urged all parties to continue prioritising the health and safety of students and school personnel in view of the current haze situation. “Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure, particularly those who are sensitive to haze conditions.

items.title: Over 400 people detained in drug raid on Jalan Sultan Ismail entertainment centre
items.summary: Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said all the arrests in the raid, which started around 2.30am, consisted of premises guards, workers and visitors, including four Bangladeshi nationals. “All those detained were brought to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters (IPD) for documentation and urine screening tests,” he said in a statement today. Meanwhile, in a separate raid, the police arrested eight individuals, including six foreigners, at another unlicensed entertainment centre on Jalan Tun Razak, around 2am earlier today.

items.title: Man, 42, dies after collapsing during running event in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — A 42-year-old man died while participating in a running event here early this morning. Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said the victim was reported to have collapsed while participating in the event before being taken to the Putrajaya Hospital’s emergency department at around 6.52am. “The Putrajaya Hospital authorities tried to resuscitate the victim, but their efforts were unsuccessful and the victim was pronounced dead at 6.54am.

items.title: Guar Chempedak assemblyman, son injured after SUV overturns in Yan crash
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 1 — Guar Chempedak state assemblyman Abdul Ghafar Saad and his son sustained minor injuries after the sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in collided with a car in Ulu Sedaka, near Yan, yesterday. Yan deputy district police chief DSP Aikap Dunding said police received information about the accident, which happened in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Ulu Sedaka, at 8.41am. He said the Proton X50 SUV was driven by the 32-year-old son of the Guar Chempedak assemblyman, while Abdul Ghafar was a passenger in the vehicle.

items.title: Campaign ‘flag war’ begins in Melaka as parties stretch limited election budgets
items.summary: Several political parties are reusing flags from previous state elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan for the Melaka polls. Political party flags line the roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. Political party flags are being put up along roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026.

items.title: Fahmi: Three more Asean countries keen to join Malaysia-led children’s online safety push
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Thailand, Brunei and Cambodia are the latest Asean countries to have expressed interest in joining Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore in efforts to address online safety issues involving children. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he welcomed the development, describing it as a sign that Asean was moving in the same direction. Also present was Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.

items.title: BN banks on five-year track record to win fence-sitters at Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is confident that the achievements and performance of the state administration over the past five years will be among the key factors considered by fence-sitters in determining their choice of candidate in the Melaka state election on November 14. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said these voters would assess the party based on its ability to administer the state, as well as the effectiveness of policies and initiatives that directly benefit the people. Ab Rauf, who is also Chief Minister, said approaches taken by the state government to win over the group included the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR), Hari Exco Bertemu Rakyat and Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programmes, which focus on identifying and resolving various issues faced by the people.

items.title: Melaka polls: MCMC won’t interfere in parties’ social media campaigns, will only act on complaints
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by contesting political parties during the 16th Melaka State Election, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts concerning campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms,” he said when asked about MCMC’s online monitoring measures during the Melaka polls scheduled for November 14. Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC is also monitoring the misuse of social media accounts to spread false information, the use of deepfakes, and extremely offensive content.

items.title: Anwar among racing buffs in Sepang to watch Marquez win Malaysian MotoGP
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today spent time watching the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here. Today’s race saw Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez strengthen his position at the summit of the 2026 MotoGP world championship after emerging as the champion, followed by Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in second place and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP in third. The victory saw Marc Marquez collect 399 points, thereby widening the gap to 44 points over his closest challenger, Jorge Martin of Aprilia Racing, who now has 355 points.

items.title: Azalina: All 218 MPs get a role in reforms under CSA as AG-PP split, PM term limit need cross-party support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Cross-party cooperation through the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) is important in building parliamentary consensus to advance institutional reforms in the country, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. In this regard, she welcomed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s support for the implementation of the CSA, as well as his proposal to extend the cooperation to more opposition parties. Azalina said that as part of the Unity Government, Barisan Nasional (BN) would continue to play a constructive role in maintaining political stability, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring the country’s administration functions effectively in the interests of the people.

items.title: Zahid: Rural and Regional Development Ministry aims to clear RM259.5m in project arrears by year-end
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes that outstanding payments for projects under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) can be resolved amicably by the end of this year. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts would be made to ensure payments for completed projects that had yet to be settled, including progress payments due to contractors and suppliers, could be made. “We will endeavour to ensure that funds are made available to settle payments for projects that have been completed but remain unpaid, as well as progress payments due to contractors and suppliers.

items.title: BN ready to invite Perikatan to join state govt if it wins Melaka polls, says Zahid
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional (PN) to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026 .

items.title: Four dead as cars veer into oncoming lanes in separate KL, Johor crashes
items.summary: In an accident involving a Perodua Myvi and a Toyota Vellfire at Kilometer 23 of the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2), near Bukit Antarabangsa, early this morning, two men were killed. Kulai district police chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the accident involving a Toyota Vios and a Mazda at about 2.30pm.

items.title: Sarawak explores collaboration with Russia on rocket, satellite launches, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 1 — The Sarawak government is exploring potential collaboration with Russia in rocket and satellite launches, leveraging the state’s strategic location near the Equator. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the proposal was raised by the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Malaysia, Naiyl M. Latypov, during a courtesy call last week. Abang Johari said Sarawak must capitalise on growing international interest in the state by implementing effective policies and ensuring clear development plans.

items.title: AGC files appeal, weighs bid to reinstate murder charge against senior Perak cop in student hit-and-run case
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is considering whether to seek the reinstatement of a murder charge against a senior police officer in the case involving the death of student Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie, following the officer’s conviction on a lesser charge of causing death. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the AGC had filed an appeal at the Court of Appeal last week against the Ipoh High Court’s decision, but was still examining the various aspects of the case before deciding on the arguments to be submitted. On October 28, the Ipoh High Court sentenced DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, 47, to seven years and six months’ imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to an amended charge of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, three years ago.

items.title: Immigration Dept: Report special pass irregularities directly to us or MACC
items.summary: Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said information or evidence could be submitted to JIM or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to facilitate a comprehensive investigation. “Providing information directly to the authorities is crucial to protecting the confidentiality of information and preserving the integrity of evidence. Zakaria said JIM welcomed information on alleged misconduct by its officers and would ensure that all reports received were reviewed and referred for appropriate action under the prevailing laws and regulations.

items.title: Brace for the toughest GE yet: Loke warns DAP as BN and Perikatan close ranks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP must prepare for its toughest general election yet as growing cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) threatens to upend the country’s political landscape, Anthony Loke said today. Addressing delegates at the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territories DAP annual convention today, Loke urged members to cast aside complacency and tighten the party’s machinery ahead of the 16th general election (GE16). DAP’s core objective in Kuala Lumpur remains retaining all five parliamentary seats secured during the 15th general election (GE15).
